$comment: Per-browser command-line flag overrides for GPU/compositing fixes.
Source of truth for browsers-gpu.nix — a Nix module that wraps any
declared browser package with these flags. To add a NEW browser:
just add an entry under `browsers` — wrapper auto-applies on next switch.
Evidence (2026-04-29 chrome://gpu + 8 isolated-profile probes):
Native Wayland mode (default on Plasma 6 / KWin) produces:
- 'Failed to find drm render node path'
- 'Compositing: Software only. Hardware acceleration disabled'
- 'eglCreateContext: Requested version is not supported'
- chrome://gpu Problems: 'Gpu compositing has been disabled'
Chromium's OWN error suggests the fix:
- probe 04 stderr: '--ozone-platform=wayland is not compatible with
Vulkan. Consider switching to --ozone-platform=x11'
Probes 06 + 08 with --ozone-platform=x11 produced ZERO GPU errors.
XWayland path delivers a working DRM render node to Chromium-family
browsers via KWin's mature XWayland integration. Native Wayland may
work in a future Chromium/KWin release — flag is easy to remove here.
Schema:
browsers.<binname>.flags     extra args appended to every launch
browsers.<binname>.rationale why this flag set is needed (for grep)

brave.rationale: (1) --ozone-platform=x11: KDE Plasma 6 / KWin Wayland fails to deliver DRM render node to Chromium 147 — force XWayland for hardware compositing. (2) --disable-features=AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL: under x11 mode, Tiger Lake's VAAPI hardware video decode path triggers PIPELINE_ERROR_DECODE on H.264 (verified 2026-04-29 via CDP probe of background3.mp4). Falling back to CPU video decode is cheap on i5-1135G7 and lets H.264/H.265 videos actually play; GPU still does compositing/raster (the main win). (3) userDataDir is separate so the GPU variant launches as independent process from the unwrapped brave (Chromium's singleton lock is per-data-dir); brave.nix symlinks shared config back from the original profile.

$exclude_comment: DO NOT add `chromium` here. The chromium nixpkgs package exposes a
desktop, etc.) depend on. symlinkJoin destroys `.override`, so
wrapping chromium breaks the entire electron build. Brave/Chrome/
Vivaldi are leaf packages — safe to wrap.
